tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. On Windows this bash is Git-Bash (MSYS2), not WSL: drives appear as `/c/...`, Windows executables run directly, and Linux-only tools are missing — use the `wsl` tool for a real Linux distribution. For PowerShell use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7, cross-platform) or, on Windows only, `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1). Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Background execution is not available; long-running commands must finish within the timeout.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path is resolved against it.

envs.description: Environment variables to set for this command (object of string values). `DSH_*` keys are ignored.

tools.name: bash_persistent
tools.description: Run commands in a persistent bash shell. State, including the current directory and exported environment variables, persists across calls for this agent. On Windows this bash is Git-Bash (MSYS2), not WSL; use `pwsh_persistent` for a persistent PowerShell session.

command.description: The bash command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a local image file (PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP/PBM/TGA/TIFF/WEBP/EXR/QOI/ICO/CUR/ANI) and return the image itself to the model. Images whose long edge exceeds 2000px are downscaled automatically; the result states the original size and the coordinate multiplier.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved like the read tool (relative paths use the session working directory). Extension-less files are identified by their content.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell 7 command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use the host's native form (`C:\...` on Windows); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. pwsh is cross-platform PowerShell 7; on Windows prefer it over `powershell` (Windows PowerShell 5.1) unless a command needs 5.1-only modules or COM. On Linux/macOS native commands and paths are case-sensitive, and `ls`/`cat`/`curl` are the real executables rather than aliases. Use `bash` for POSIX shell syntax and `wsl` for a Linux distribution on Windows. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$env:DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Background execution is not available; long-running commands must finish within the timeout.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session working directory; a relative path is resolved against it.

envs.description: Environment variables to set for this command (object of string values). `DSH_*` keys are ignored.

tools.name: pwsh_persistent
tools.description: Run PowerShell 7 (`pwsh`) commands in a persistent session. State, including the current location, variables, functions, imported modules and `$env:` changes, persists across calls for this agent. All output streams are merged into one text result. A failed command ends with `[exit code: N]`: N is the exit code of the last native command when it failed, otherwise 1 when the last statement reported an error or a terminating error was thrown. `exit` ends the session and the next call starts a fresh one. Use `pwsh` for a one-off command, `bash_persistent` for persistent POSIX shell state, and `powershell` (Windows only) when Windows PowerShell 5.1 is required.

command.description: The PowerShell command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

tools.name: str_replace_editor
tools.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted. Required parameters still need values; omit `str_replace.new_str` rather than setting it to null when deleting a match

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required string parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

insert_line.description: Required integer parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

new_str.description: Optional string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if omitted, no string will be added). Required string parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. A null placeholder is accepted only by commands that do not use this parameter.

old_str.description: Required string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If omitted or null, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: working_directory
tools.description: Read the current working directory, or change it with cd. Relative paths in file tools and newly started shells and terminals resolve against it. Existing persistent shells and terminals keep their own directories. The write permission root stays at the session's original directory: writing outside it, or starting a shell outside it, needs user approval.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter, absolute or relative to the current directory. Omit to read the current directory.

tools.name: create_worktree
tools.description: Create a new Git branch and worktree from a local commit, branch, or tag, then change this session's working directory to it. The checkout goes to <current checkout root>/.agents/worktrees/<name>. Defaults to HEAD and a generated name; no fetch is performed. Uncommitted files stay in the source checkout. Existing branch names or checkout paths fail. Use working_directory with cd to leave; the checkout and branch remain.

name.description: New branch name, also used as the checkout directory. Omit to generate a unique name.

from.description: Local commit, branch, or tag to start from. Defaults to HEAD.
